answer: Anti-Sybil via comet-window island TEEs: each identity binds to one hardware island that issues a quill-stamped remote-attestation quote. Auditors accept only quotes whose PCR set matches a registered enclave and whose freshness falls inside a short comet window. Extra identities each need a separate island enclave—clones on one host collide on the single TEE quote, so splitting cannot share attestation capacity. Limitation: cloud TEE fleets still scale linearly, and a broken TEE needs fast quote revocation.
